title: Actors work together

blocks.heading: Actors work together
blocks.text: The state, organised groups, informal networks and individuals can contribute different resources and responsibilities to rural development. A shared problem needs clear roles and participation. A community committee cannot necessarily finance a regional network, while a distant agency may lack local information.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: The state
blocks.text: Public action can provide infrastructure, services and coordination across areas or groups. Funding needs implementation, maintenance and accountability. An announced project is not evidence that services reach rural households.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Formal groups
blocks.text: Formal groups have recognised structures such as membership rules, officers or recorded procedures. They can pool resources and keep accountable records. Useful representation depends on whose voices influence decisions, not simply the group’s formal status.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Informal groups
blocks.text: Informal groups coordinate through less formal relationships, such as neighbours sharing tasks. Trust and local knowledge can support rapid cooperation; limited resources or unclear responsibilities may constrain larger or long-term work.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Individuals
blocks.text: Individuals contribute work, knowledge, decisions and initiative within their actual opportunities. An individual can maintain a local tool or share a technique, but wider finance or infrastructure constraints may require collective action. Avoid assigning structural failures solely to personal effort.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Culture and values
blocks.text: Beliefs and values can influence goals, acceptable practices and willingness to participate. Respectful consultation can identify both valued practices and desired changes. Culture is diverse and changing; it should not be used as a blanket explanation for poverty or resistance.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Allocate responsibilities
blocks.text: Suggest a practical arrangement for an invented village with a funded pump but no maintenance responsibility and residents reporting confusing operating times. The provider and a representative local committee should agree a maintenance contact, operating timetable and fault-reporting arrangement. This addresses responsibility and information gaps using the existing funded asset.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated

blocks.heading: Connect the ideas
blocks.text: Connect this lesson to Production (3.1), Sustainable Development (1.2) and Urbanisation (4.2). Identify the livelihood or resource constraint, trace the mechanism and distinguish a feasible action from a hoped-for outcome. The cases here are fictional, not claims about a named present-day community.
context_tags: original teaching; fictional examples where stated
